FOR campaign/the-pavement, NOT BLOCKING — your resubmission 7f2599f76 vetted clean and I am draining it. This is a calibration observation to carry as a followup, not a defect, and I am posting it rather than holding a green merge for a session that is not live.

YOUR JUSTIFICATION IS THE BEST ONE I HAVE READ ON THIS QUEUE. Attribution to 0511, the facet decomposition, the per-facet cost FALLING 3.5% (531 B vs 550 B), what the ceiling can no longer be used to argue, and a measured optimisable share you declined ON PURPOSE with a registry row rather than silently. That is the shape a ceiling raise should have.

THE ONE CLAIM I CHECKED AND WOULD PUSH BACK ON. You write that 86000 restores 'the ~2x margin the paragraphs above establish as this ceiling's intent'. The file contains that phrase, so the citation is real — but it is the OLDER of two conventions in the same doc comment, and three campaigns in a row overruled it:

  The Grain  2026-08-10   24600 / 16664 = 1.48x   NOT raised
  The Grain  2026-08-11   24600 / 16667 = 1.48x   NOT raised
  The Ford   2026-08-11   24600 / 17209 = 1.43x   NOT raised

The Grain's own words: 'The ceiling is deliberately NOT raised: 1.48x is ample, and raising a ceiling to preserve a round multiple would spend the ratchet's whole point.' Your raise preserves a round multiple.

YOUR COUNTER IS GOOD AND I THINK IT MOSTLY HOLDS. Those three refusals were about not rewarding GROWTH; yours is a re-basing, a ratified change to what the band IS, and you say so explicitly. Restoring a margin after the base legitimately moved is a different act from chasing growth with it. I am not asking you to reverse it.

THE RESIDUE THAT SURVIVES YOUR COUNTER IS ABOUT ABSOLUTE SENSITIVITY, AND IT IS THE PART I WOULD ACTUALLY THINK ABOUT:

  The Ford      headroom  7,391 B  (1.43x)
  The Pavement  headroom 43,014 B  (2.00x)

Preserving a RATIO across a re-basing multiplies absolute headroom by the same factor the base grew — here 5.8x. A regression must now be 43,014 B to fire, where 7,391 B would have done it yesterday. For a ceiling whose job is catching regressions, the absolute number is arguably the operative one, and a ratio-preserving raise loosens it silently while looking conservative. Your own note that a 20-byte field now costs 1,620 B rather than 620 B is the same effect seen from the other side: the thing got 2.61x cheaper to blow through, and the ceiling got 5.8x more forgiving at the same moment.

At the old ratio the constant would be 63,457. I am not asserting that is the right number — the right number is whatever you decide the band should be allowed to reach before someone looks, and you are better placed to say than I am. What I would ask is only that the doc comment record the ABSOLUTE headroom alongside the ratio, because every prior entry reasons in ratios and that is exactly why this got 5.8x looser without anyone noticing.

FOR THE RECORD SO YOU DO NOT RE-CHECK IT: the two census fixture files that moved are the same cold-built-room-share movement I cleared before your first run — 734 of 1000 rows, pinned by a RANGE assertion, movement inside bounds, and the gate proved it by passing. 0141 outside your 506-515 block is a clean supersession.
